subject: HelioHealth renewal: usage drift and tiering recommendation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: HelioHealth renewal: usage drift and tiering recommendation

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled a short usage health snapshot covering Q1–Q2 2027 and wanted to surface two items ahead of the renewal conversation: token spend drift and a recommended tiering adjustment to improve unit economics.

Key points (summary):
- Net token consumption up ~48% QoQ driven by an increase in short chat sessions and a new batch document-classification job that spikes nightly.
- Average p50 latency for the main chat endpoint remains at ~180ms; p95 moved from 420ms to 520ms during the peak window (2–4am PST).
- Without commit changes, the current per-token blended rate will push FY spend ~22% over forecast by month 9.

I attached a CSV with the per-route breakdown and a short PDF with our recommended tiering (short-term burst add-on + medium-term 12-month commit rebalance) that reduces blended unit cost by ~18% while keeping peak headroom.

Would you be available next Tue (Apr 6) for a 30-min alignment with procurement? If procurement prefers a written mutual action plan first, I can draft one with timeline/milestones.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth renewal: usage drift and tiering recommendation

Irene —

Thanks for the quick summary and attached files. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock time with procurement:
1) That 48% jump — is it normalized for the new nightly batch job we turned on Feb 15? We were expecting some uplift but want to separate steady-state chat growth vs batch jobs.
2) The p95 latency increase during off-hours — does that reflect overloaded shared capacity or a model-size mismatch? Our SRE is especially sensitive to anything above 500ms.

Procurement is out next week, so written MAP would be ideal. Can you include an explicit timeline for DocuSign steps and a proposed billing cadence?

—Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Product Ops | HelioHealth
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth renewal: usage drift and tiering recommendation

Samira — great questions. Quick answers here and I attached the CSV that flags batch vs interactive token mix.

1) The 48% is total consumption. When we isolate the nightly batch job (enabled Feb 15) it accounts for ~21 percentage points of the increase. The remaining ~27% comes from organic chat volume (new cohort of triage users) and an increase in assistant-initiated follow-ups.

2) The p95 latency bump is primarily driven by resource contention on burst windows — shared-hosted routing saw a queueing spike. We validated with our infra team: model SKU is still appropriate for accuracy needs; this is operational headroom, not a model-size mismatch. For Helio we recommend a short-term burst reservation to flatten the p95 and then a move to a Dedicated lane for the nightly job if Helio wants isolation.

I put together a one-page mutual action plan that lays out milestones:
- Week 1: Agree on commit size and burst add-on (if any).
- Week 2: Sign MSA addendum + DocuSign.
- Week 3–4: Provision burst capacity and baseline monitoring.
- 30–60 days: Evaluate Dedicated migration for nightly batch if ROI targets met.

I'll draft the MAP and send for your review this afternoon. Looping Dylan for pricing details and Marissa for ROI snapshots.

Irene
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Pricing note — HelioHealth proposed tiering and commit options

Hi Samira — Dylan here (renewals). Thanks for the details. Short pricing note to put numbers next to the MAP: 

Option A — Short-term burst + 12-month rebalance (recommended)
- New 12-month commit: $120k/month (upfront billing option available)
- Included burst add-on: 2x peak capacity for 90 days, $12k one-time provisioning fee
- Estimated blended token price: $0.00415 (18% savings vs current blended rate)

Option B — No commit, burst-only (transitional)
- Month-to-month + burst usage metered; expected FY spend +12% vs current forecast
- Blended token price remains higher (~$0.0051) but no long-term commitment

Option C — Dedicated lane for nightly batch (12-month)
- Dedicated GPU pool sized for nightly job: $45k/month + support tier upgrade (recommended for isolation)
- Expected latency p95 reduction to <300ms for batch windows; total blended economics depend on commit size across chat and batch.

I'll attach a short ROI slide that models monthly spend vs savings and a suggested PO template for procurement. Happy to walk through numbers on a call.

—Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: ROI snapshot + monitoring guardrails

Samira — attaching the ROI snapshot (pptx) and a short checklist for SRE to validate quality regression risk post-migration. Highlights: 
- Breakeven on the 12-month rebalance occurs at month 4 assuming current growth curve and stable batch duty cycle.
- Predicted token cost savings (12-month commit + burst): ~$260k versus status quo across 12 months.
- Monitoring guardrails: token-level cost alerts, p95 latency SLO hooks, and an automated fallback to hosted model variants during Dedicated provisioning windows.

Suggested next steps for your team:
1) Review ROI slide with procurement — mark any questions directly in the Drive file.
2) Confirm whether Helio prefers PO/Net30 vs upfront billing (we can adapt pricing and incentives).
3) If procurement wants a Dedicated pilot for the nightly job, tell us target throughput and we'll size the pool.

Cheers,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@heliohealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth renewal: usage drift and tiering recommendation

Team — thanks for the clear options and the MAP. Procurement reviewed the ROI slide and prefers Option A with upfront billing if we can get a 30-day pilot window on the burst add-on before full commit. They also want the MAP with explicit DocuSign milestones.

Irene — can you send the written MAP + DocuSign link today? Procurement email is procurement@heliohealth.com and they want a PO-ready summary. Assuming those items look good, we can target signature by Apr 20.

—Samira
